non_goals: Adding a new dedicated live test file unless implementation proves client/main_test.odin cannot stay coherent.
Adding GUI automation, container orchestration, or a broader cross-platform release matrix.
Revalidating protocol slices already covered by existing common/server/client tests.
Using PostgreSQL bootstrap identities as the auth-semantic source of truth.

conventions: Prefer one bounded live proof plus existing baselines over a monolithic integration suite.
Use client/main_test.odin as the live-proof anchor unless a concrete blocker emerges during implementation.
Keep failures attributable to startup, connect, auth, or message exchange.
Treat Linux-first support as a local developer confidence gate statement, not a release-wide platform claim.

hard: Scope stays limited to automated startup/auth/one-message MVP coverage.
Baseline odin test common, odin test server, and odin test client remain part of the gate.
Prefer focused headless harnesses over GUI or broad infrastructure work.
Failures must map cleanly to startup, connect, auth, or message exchange.
Do not rely on PostgreSQL bootstrap identities for auth semantics.
soft: Extend client/main_test.odin rather than adding a new live test file.
Keep Windows scope out of slice for HC-118 unless a trivial supported path already exists.
compatibility: The existing live seam is testClientServerTransportCanEstablishLiveStartupAuthOverENet in client/main_test.odin.
run-test-server.sh currently owns bootstrap/start but lacks readiness waiting, background lifecycle control, and guaranteed cleanup.
HC-107 startup behavior already ties successful startup to database-ready/preflighted usability.
Current server routing remains chat-only and ignores non-chat channels for MVP traffic.
security_requirements: Reuse encrypted transport helpers instead of bypassing auth or packet sealing.
Keep helper credentials environment-driven and local-only in scope.
Do not expose secrets in failure output.

patterns: Client tests already mix reducer-only coverage with an opt-in live ENet seam in one file.
Server-side live orchestration is script-owned rather than embedded in test code.
Startup usability is already treated as a readiness contract, not just a spawned process.

gotchas.text: The current helper has no explicit readiness wait or guaranteed background cleanup, so naively composing it into a gate will produce timing and orphan-process failures.
The live seam is opt-in through HAYCHAT_LIVE_STARTUP_AUTH=1, so the gate must deliberately enable and isolate that path.
Linux-first support must be documented as local confidence only; otherwise reviewers may infer cross-platform coverage that the slice does not provide.
HC-118 is complete at the documented code-and-docs scope even if a given local machine still fails the gate because the configured PostgreSQL user lacks permission on schema public during bootstrap.

security_considerations.concern: Live tests must reuse the real encrypted packet helpers instead of shortcutting auth or packet sealing.
Defaults are acceptable for local Linux gating only and should remain environment-overridable.

testing_patterns.test_organization: Package-local _test.odin files with one opt-in live client seam and broad slice coverage elsewhere.
mock_patterns: Runtime helper reuse instead of GUI driving

domain_context.error_handling: HC-118 acceptance requires distinct startup, connect, auth, and message failure attribution rather than one opaque integration error.
domain_context.data_flow: local bootstrap/start helper -> ready server -> client A startup auth -> client B startup auth -> client A encrypted room-chat send -> server routes chat-only message -> client B runtime service receives authoritative event
